title: Circle Theorems

problems_fixed.what: Duplicate solution within tier (was 90, same as bronze[2] semicircle). Repaired into a tangent-radius + triangle-sum problem yielding a distinct clean answer.

old.display: A tangent meets a radius. What is the angle between them?

new.display: Tangent at T, O centre; angle at T (tangent meets radius) = 90 and angle at O = 55; find angle at P.

problems_fixed.what: Wrong quantity AND duplicate (stored 40 = angle at centre, but question asks the angle between the two tangents = 140; also duplicated silver[0]=40). Reworded to give PO=70 with each tangent; angle between tangents = 2x70 = 140.

Degenerate cyclic quadrilateral: angles 3x,4x,5x,6x in cyclic order cannot all lie on a circle (opposite pairs 3x+5x=180 gives x=22.5 but 4x+6x=180 gives x=18, contradiction). Replaced with a single valid opposite-pair constraint.

old.display: A cyclic quadrilateral has angles 3x, 4x, 5x, and 6x. Find x.
old.note: answer 20 only from sum=360, ignoring the cyclic constraint

new.display: A cyclic quadrilateral has one pair of opposite angles equal to 4x and 5x. Find x.

problems_fixed.what: Muddled wording ('Angle in a semicircle plus another angle = 180') reworded for clarity; answer unchanged.
Ambiguous 'Angle ATB (B on circle, same side)' clarified to the standard alternate-segment statement (angle TBA with B on the major arc); answer unchanged.

misconceptions_rewritten: All 20 problems: original 'misconceptions' were worked solutions with no expect key and several contained em dashes (validator + honest-diagnosis failures). Replaced with derivable honest-diagnosis misconceptions, each expect committed by simulating the exact error (e.g. bronze0 double-not-halve=200, silver0 used-360=85, silver2 gave-centre-angle=40, gold0 forgot-factor-2=3, gold3 added-not-multiplied=7, gold4 chord-part-confusion=26). silver[4] (equal tangents) has no determinate numeric error -> empty misconceptions.
guided_added: tier_guides (bronze/silver/gold), tier descriptions, guided.opener, guided.teach.{bronze,silver,gold}, and guided_steps + hint on all 20 bank problems. Every guided box value recomputed independently and lands on the stored solution; completion boundary (phase:substitute) set so the set-up is pre-worked and the solve-through + check stay live (>=2 boxes).
opener_concept: Two guides in a circular gallery look at the same painting on the curved wall; from the centre it fills 80 degrees, from the wall exactly half. Halving 80 to 40 by common sense IS the angle-at-centre-is-twice-the-circumference theorem; the reveal names it and notes the semicircle special case (180 -> 90).
